# Best portable power stations for camping

For most campers, a 250-500Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, camera batteries and a CPAP. Step up in size only if you want to run a fridge or stay off-grid for several days.

## Weekend tent or car camping (~288Wh)
- **Best overall: Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**, about $249. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4, weighs 8.3 lb and puts out 300W AC. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Best value: EcoFlow River 3 Plus**, about $269-299. It has 286Wh, a 600W inverter (double the Jackery's), and can expand to 572Wh. It weighs about 9.9 lb. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Cheapest 288Wh option: Anker SOLIX C300**, about $199. It has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC-outlet version, not the AC-less "C300 DC." ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/))
- **Budget: Bluetti EB3A**, about $179. It has 268Wh and a 600W inverter, with a basic app. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)) TechRadar's budget pick is the similar Bluetti Elite 30 V2 (288Wh, 600W). ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))

## Fridge or van camping (~1kWh)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**, about $799. It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output and weighs about 23.8 lb. TechRadar also picks it as best for camping. ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/), [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))
- **Bluetti AC180**, $499 ($474.05 with code AFF5OFF). It has 1,152Wh and an 1,800W inverter, weighs about 35 lb and has a 5-year warranty. The code was tested in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission). ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))

## Multi-day off-grid
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick, scoring 81 in its lab tests. It's listed at $1,499 but was recently on sale for under $900. It weighs 39 lb, puts out 2,200W and has easy solar add-ons. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's camping pick, at about $1,079-$1,199. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating and weighs just under 40 lb. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))

## My suggestion
If you mainly need to charge devices and run lights or a CPAP, get the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**, or the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** if you want more AC output. If you want a fridge or more days of power, get the **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** or the **Bluetti AC180**.

## Caveats
- Prices change often, and a major sales period around Black Friday is coming, so it's worth checking before you buy.
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier, since it can triple the draw.
- OutdoorGearLab scored the small units lower than the big ones (Jackery Explorer 300 at 52, Anker C300 at 50). Those scores reflect their small capacity, not poor quality for light camping use.
- The search results gave me review pages rather than direct store links, except for the Bluetti AC180. The "Check price" buttons on the [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) and [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) pages lead to the retailers.

Tell me your budget, what you need to power, and how many nights you'll be out, and I can narrow it to one pick.
